byteIdentity.method: The 0ef6970, 54a7c39 and fff58b3 skeletons run in turn from one path with one package.json: 16 argument sets (inspect/apply over ok, empty, directory, missing and protected files and 13 hostile names: ESC/SGR, an SGR 1 opener, C1 CSI, RLO, U+2028, LF, TAB, two label-shaped names, emoji, U+200E; --go, --go --yes, --note with a label-shaped value, a missing --note value, an unknown command, no path, --go on inspect, --version, --cheat, --help, -h) x 6 mode sets (human, --brief, --quiet, --json, --brief --quiet, --json --brief) x 7 environments (none, NO_COLOR=1, FORCE_COLOR=1, FORCE_COLOR=0, TERM=dumb, FORCE_COLOR=1+NO_COLOR=1, TERM=dumb+FORCE_COLOR=1) x piped and pty (stdout and stderr merge on the pty; exit read from a marker file; the pty’s echoed ^D normalised).
byteIdentity.result: 2016 runs a version. Against 0ef6970: all 980 non-human results (490 pairs, piped and pty) byte-identical in stdout, stderr and exit; human 112 byte-identical and 84 identical once SGR 1/22 and blank lines are removed, stderr and exit equal; --help differs by its header text (changed in 4c3d9b0) and is covered by the splice. Against 54a7c39: every non-human and human result byte-identical (the item renderer is untouched); every --help result identical once SGR 1/22 and blank lines are removed. No escape byte in any piped run without a forcing FORCE_COLOR; on the pty --help is bold exactly under none, FORCE_COLOR=1, FORCE_COLOR=1+NO_COLOR=1 and TERM=dumb+FORCE_COLOR=1, and plain under NO_COLOR=1, FORCE_COLOR=0 and TERM=dumb. Scaffolder at 0ef6970 and fff58b3, 13 argument sets (four modes, a bad name in three modes, an unknown flag, --version, --cheat, a control character in --author, an unwritable --dir, --brief --quiet): identical except the version string, the template byte counts in --json data and blank lines in the human run.

names: Top-level fence names added since 54a7c39: RUNTIME_HELP_TITLE (fff58b3), RUNTIME_HELP_FLAG and RUNTIME_HELP_USAGE (650a0b9); none dropped; 63 in all. ADOPTING step 1 lists all three. Scan of the 128 adopted tool files carrying the v3 fence (105 distinct headers): no top-level declaration of any fence name above or below the fence, and no mention of the three new names at all; node --check passes on a scratch copy of every one of the 128 with the fff58b3 block swapped in.
help: Every adopted header (128 files) spliced into the 54a7c39 and fff58b3 skeletons and run with --help, piped and under FORCE_COLOR=1: exit 0 and empty stderr everywhere; the non-blank lines equal the raw header’s non-blank lines in order (so equal to what 0ef6970 printed) and equal 54a7c39’s; the raw header, its own blank lines included, is a subsequence of the output, so only blank lines are added; the FORCE_COLOR=1 output unbolds to the piped text; no escape byte piped; every output opens with exactly one blank line; no run of three blank lines anywhere; every one of the 625 headings that follows content has exactly two blank lines before it and one after. Bold spans: 625 headings, 125 titles, 342 usage subcommands, 2353 entry tokens, nothing else. Usage: the tool name is never bold; every bolded subcommand read by hand against its line (273 distinct usage lines) is a real subcommand.
injection: Help text is the author’s own header and, as in 0ef6970, is not escaped; what 650a0b9/fff58b3 add is SGR 1/22 around a heading, a title token, usage words and an entry token. 20 000 random headers built from ESC/SGR fragments (1, 22, 0, 4), colons, dashes, double spaces, flags, <value>, [value], CR, U+2028, U+0085, TAB, RLO, emoji and capitals, run in-process with bold on: every output line carries as many added SGR 1 as SGR 22 (a pair never spans a line), no raw line is lost, reordered or changed but for bold, and no added blank makes a run of three where the author wrote fewer. The item renderer (escape first, then bold) is unchanged: its output is byte-identical to 54a7c39 over the 13 hostile names above.

knownLimits: Usage: the tool token is the first token of the first usage line. A Usage section that opens with prose at two spaces (`  Run it with no args to list.`) bolds `it with no` and then nothing on the real usage lines; a prose line in Usage that starts with the tool name bolds the lowercase words after it (`  t reads the config and stops` → `reads the config`); `npx t list` bolds `t list`. None of the 105 distinct real headers does this (five open with `node file.mjs …`, which bolds nothing).

A header whose first comment line is a `//` spacer opens with two blank lines, not one; a whitespace-only header line (`//` and three spaces) next to an added blank shows as three visually blank lines; a CRLF header gets no headings (the title and entries still bold). No real header has any of these (0 spacer-first, 0 whitespace-only, 0 CR).

A first line `Usage: t [opts] <file>` bolds `Usage` as the title; prose at an entry’s indent with two spaces after a one-word sentence (`  Done.  Then …`) bolds `Done.`. Neither occurs in the real headers.
